Principle 13: Politics in Korea
Korean Politics during the Seventies and Eighties
During the 1970s and 1980s, Koreans were living under a dictatorship.
Many people who believed in democracy suffered at the hands of Korea’s dictators.
After this time of authoritarian rule had passed, many citizens strove to ensure that Korea became a democracy.
Fortunately, in the late 1980’s, the Summer Olympics were held in Seoul.
This great international event helped Korea to move towards becoming a more democratic society.
The Progression of Democracy in Korea
Because Korea has been a democratic country for a short period of time, many people today still do not have a good understanding of how the political system of our country works.
Not only do some citizens not have a good understanding of democracy, but our politicians also lack this knowledge as well.
We all have a lot to learn about how to make the democratic system of government function effectively in Korea.
The Political Problems of Korea
Many Korean politicians are corrupt and accept bribes.
The two main parties of Korea, the Democrats and the Republicans, fight a lot.
These problems are not only the politician’s responsibility, but the people’s as well.
We must learn to work together to make Korea the best country it can be.
The Responsibility of Korean Citizens
As democracy in Korea continues to grow, we have to elect more honest politicians.
We must vote wisely for the politicians who we think will represent the voter fairly and support them continuously.
By voting for upright government leaders, we can put the fate of Korea in our hands.
